title: Compound and complex tenses
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Mais-que-perfeito simples
lessons.explanation: The simple pluperfect is a one-word past-before-past form, mostly literary or formal. Take the eles form of the pretérito perfeito, drop -m, and add the ending: falaram gives falara, fizeram gives fizera, disseram gives dissera, viram gives vira, saíram gives saíra, foram gives fora. The nós form takes an accent on the vowel before -ramos: faláramos, fizéramos, tivéramos. In speech the compound form (tinha falado) replaces it, but the simple form appears in writing, news and literature: quando cheguei, ele já saíra. Do not confuse it with the perfeito: saiu is a simple past, saíra is anterior to another past moment.

lessons.title: Futuro do presente composto and futuro do pretérito composto
lessons.explanation: Terá/terão + participle (futuro do presente composto) marks an event that will be complete before a future point: até sexta, eu terei terminado. Teria/teriam + participle (futuro do pretérito composto) marks what would have happened but did not: eu teria ficado, mas tinha trabalho. Both use ter as the auxiliary and the participle never changes. In speech the future perfect is often replaced by já + present (até sexta, já terminei), but the compound form is the standard written choice. Do not use the simple future where completion before a deadline is the point.

lessons.title: Futuro do subjuntivo composto: tiver + participle
lessons.explanation: The compound future subjunctive is tiver, tiveres, tiver, tivermos, tiverem + participle. It appears after se, quando, assim que, depois que and logo que when an action will be finished before the main verb: quando você tiver terminado, me ligue. The simple future subjunctive (quando você terminar) only says the two events happen around the same time; the compound form insists on completion first. The main clause is in the future, present or imperative. Do not use the perfeito do subjuntivo (tenha) after these conjunctions, and do not use the imperfect (tivesse): they belong to other constructions.

lessons.title: Aspect periphrases: acabar de, voltar a, deixar de, costumar, vir + gerund
lessons.explanation: Auxiliary verbs plus an infinitive or gerund express aspect, how an action unfolds. Acabar de + infinitive means to have just done something: acabei de chegar. Voltar a + infinitive means to do again: ela voltou a estudar. Deixar de + infinitive means to stop: ele deixou de fumar. Costumar + infinitive means to do habitually: eu costumo acordar cedo. Ir + gerund shows gradual progress (a situação vai melhorando), vir + gerund shows an action that has been going on up to now (vem melhorando desde 2020), and andar + gerund shows repeated or scattered activity (ela anda reclamando muito). Each verb takes its own link word or none: voltar a, deixar de, acabar de, costumar with no preposition.

lessons.title: Change of state: ficar, tornar-se, virar, passar a
lessons.explanation: Portuguese has no single verb for become; it chooses by type of change. Ficar + adjective marks a state reached, often temporary or emotional: ela ficou nervosa, ele ficou rico. Tornar-se + noun or adjective marks a lasting or formal change: ele se tornou um escritor famoso. Virar + noun is the informal choice for a change of role or form: a casa virou um museu, ele virou médico. Passar a + infinitive marks the start of a new habit or situation: passamos a morar aqui em 2020. Do not use ficar with a profession (ele ficou médico is wrong in this sense) and do not use ficar directly with an infinitive (ficamos morar is wrong).

examples.en: She got nervous at the news.
